entries.title: 📺 The television question: {client}
entries.text:
[i]“Thirty-nine episodes a year, a sponsor with deep pockets, and a face America invites into its living room every Thursday. We want {client}.”[/i]

A network offer, in writing. Steady money against silver-screen mystique — the question every agent in town is suddenly being asked.

choices.label: Sign the series — steady money, smaller screen

effects.text: {client} signs a television series — steady money, and Thursday nights belong to the sponsor.

choices.outcome: The contract is thick and the money is real. From now on {client} is furniture in a million living rooms — beloved, familiar, and a little less like a movie star every week.

choices.label: Decline — the movies are the movies

effects.text: {client} turns television down. The mystique stays on the big screen.

choices.outcome: You send regrets on good paper. Scarcity is a strategy too — as long as the picture offers keep coming.

entries.title: 📺 Season one: {client}
entries.text: The ratings are in: {client}'s show owns its time slot. The fan mail comes in sacks now — addressed to the character, mostly. The studios have noticed both facts.

quest.step: Ride out season one of {client}'s show

choices.label: Lean in — press tour, covers, the whole circus

effects.text: {client} leans into television stardom. America approves, loudly.

choices.outcome: TV Guide, supermarket openings, a catchphrase people shout across parking lots. It is not cinema. It is enormous.

choices.label: Keep one foot in pictures — negotiate hiatus windows

effects.text: Hiatus windows secured: {client} can still shoot pictures between seasons.

choices.outcome: The network grumbles and signs. {client} stays a movie face that happens to do television — the rarest trick of the decade.

effects_fail.text: The network refuses hiatus windows — {client} belongs to Thursday nights now.

choices.outcome_fail: The network holds the line: thirty-nine episodes leave room for nothing. The lot starts casting around {client}'s schedule — which means: around {client}.
